## Reviewer focus

Please review this as a targeted port from the previous Android branch, not as a UI parity rewrite. The main things to look at are:

- Android CI/Gradle gates and local mint setup: check that the new tasks and workflow jobs are appropriately scoped and do not make flaky local/native mint coverage mandatory beyond the intended gates.
- App lock and privacy: verify the secure window/privacy cover/app-lock flow does not block normal startup, onboarding, or biometric fallback behavior.
- Staged restore: focus on wallet replacement/rollback safety, restore staying inside onboarding until completion, and retry/skip/partial-success behavior per mint.
- Cashu Request changes: check request-store persistence, listener error redaction, duplicate payment suppression, quote-id attachment, mint selection, BOLT11 fallback, add-mint-and-pay, and top-up routing.
- CDK robustness: verify token receive/fee/spendability behavior stays unit-aware and fails closed for malformed or foreign tokens.
- Tests: make sure the new JVM, instrumentation, accessibility, back-navigation, and macrobenchmark coverage matches current main UI labels and does not reintroduce old branch-only UI assumptions.

## QA wallet checklist

Please smoke-test the current Android wallet flows that this PR touches:

- Fresh install and existing wallet launch: app opens, secure window/app lock behavior feels normal, privacy cover appears only when expected.
- Onboarding create wallet: create a wallet, add or skip first mints, enter the wallet, then close/reopen the app.
- Restore wallet: restore with a seed, enter multiple mint URLs, confirm each mint shows progress, and try retry/skip on a failing mint. Confirm partial restore still lets the user open the wallet once work is complete.
- Mint management/local mint basics: add a mint, refresh balance, create a receive quote, mint received funds, and confirm history updates.
- Send Lightning: paste/scan a BOLT11 invoice, review fee/total, pay if funded, and confirm failure messaging is user-safe when it cannot pay.
- Receive ecash token: paste/scan a token, review amount/fee, claim it, and confirm pending/claimed history behaves normally.
- Send ecash token: generate a token, use back navigation from generated state, and confirm pending token status checks still behave.
- Cashu Request receive: create a request, receive a payment against it, and verify duplicate notifications/payments do not double-count.
- Cashu Request pay: test compatible funded mint, incompatible requested mint with Lightning fallback, requested mint not yet added, insufficient compatible mint balance/top-up state, amountless request, and unsupported unit messaging.
- Navigation/accessibility: use Android back from overlays/sheets/status states, try large font size, and run TalkBack over balance, QR, number pad delete, transaction rows, and settings toggles.

Known validation note: local Gradle commands were not run in the implementation environment because no Java runtime was available there; CI should be the source of truth for the Android Gradle matrix.

### Visual findings

- **The clearest frame is iPhone 11 (414 pt — the largest iPhone viewport bucket).** Before, the hardcoded break still split `Pick your` / `first mint.` with roughly 100 pt of unused width. After, it renders on one line.
- **Android `+ Add custom mint URL` moves from flush-left at the 28 dp inset to centered**, matching iOS, and gains the 0.6 pressed-alpha it previously had no press feedback for.
- **Row 2 becomes Chorus OFF Mint** with its logo resolving on both platforms — no monogram fallback, so the hand-picked icon URL works.
- **Accepted trade-off:** at 360 dp the break moves from `Pick your` / `first mint.` to `Pick your first` / `mint.`, an orphan. That is the cost of removing the hardcoded break.
- **Intentional non-change:** the welcome headline keeps its break. Its iOS before/after frames are **pixel-identical** (verified by decoding PNG scanline filters, not byte hashes), proving the exception was restored exactly.
- **Android `Got it` CTA no longer clips.** The concept sheet's content was an unscrolled `Column` inside a `ModalBottomSheet` at its partially-expanded detent, so once headline + three paragraphs + button stacked taller than that detent the button fell outside the sheet and the gesture pill drew across it. Reproduced at 360×800 dp and at 411×914 dp with font_scale 1.3; 393×873 dp at 1.0 had just enough room to hide it. iOS never had it — `conceptSheet` puts a `Spacer()` ahead of the button. Fixed by giving Android the same shape and skipping the partial detent. **This was a pre-existing defect, not caused by the headline change**: before the fix the CTA band was byte-identical across this branch's first two commits.
- **iOS concept sheet now sizes to its content.** It sat at a fixed `.medium` detent — a fraction of the *screen*, not of the copy — with a `Spacer()` above the CTA soaking up the remainder. The copy-to-button gap was therefore residue that grew with device height: ~107pt on iPhone 17e, ~115pt on iPhone 17, ~134pt on iPhone 11. Measured sheet height went from **479pt / 459pt** (iPhone 11 / iPhone 17 — tracking the screen) to **381.0pt / 380.7pt** (tracking the content). The gap is now 24pt by construction everywhere. This also removes a parity gap the Android CTA fix had opened, since that sheet already hugged its content.
- **Pre-existing divergence, not fixed here:** at large accessibility text the Android headline does not grow (glyphs measure identically at font_scale 1.0 and 1.3 while body text goes 2→3 lines) because Android 14+ non-linear font scaling caps large display text, whereas iOS Dynamic Type grows the headline and changes its wrap. ## Cross-platform backup/restore parity review

Reviewed the exact range `b79f1996bc7cfb912882800cae082cb90615befc` (true merge-base) → `564ae1428f4301f306683b4482ba7d87e22ac340` (PR head). I audited both the new Android implementation and the unchanged iOS iCloud implementation as the parity control.

The PR moves Android materially closer to iOS: the seed + mint-list payload, restore write barrier, all-or-nothing mint recovery, onboarding method chooser, settings hierarchy, immediate backup on enable, wallet/mint change triggers, and local-delete/remote-preserve behavior are all deliberately paired. The different Drive/Block Store trust model is also disclosed rather than presented as equivalent to iCloud Keychain.

I found these remaining/new gaps:

1. **[P1] Disabling backup does not reliably remove the remote seed and can race with a write.** [`setEnabled(false)` turns the flag off and calls an unserialized, best-effort delete](https://github.com/cashubtc/wallet/blob/564ae1428f4301f306683b4482ba7d87e22ac340/android/app/src/main/java/com/cashu/me/Core/GoogleDriveBackupService.kt#L275-L313), while [`performBackup` only owns `backupMutex` and never re-checks `host.backupEnabled` inside it](https://github.com/cashubtc/wallet/blob/564ae1428f4301f306683b4482ba7d87e22ac340/android/app/src/main/java/com/cashu/me/Core/GoogleDriveBackupService.kt#L179-L228). An in-flight/queued upload can therefore create/update Drive or Block Store after disable has cleared it. Separately, if silent authorization returns `NeedsResolution` or deletion fails, `clearBackupData` still clears local metadata and returns no failure, even though [the confirmation says the backup “will be removed”](https://github.com/cashubtc/wallet/blob/564ae1428f4301f306683b4482ba7d87e22ac340/android/app/src/main/java/com/cashu/me/ui/settings/DriveBackupScreen.kt#L274-L290). This is especially important because the Android Drive copy contains a spendable seed without end-to-end encryption. Serialize disable/delete against uploads, re-check enabled under the same lock, and surface/retain a deletion-pending or failed state.

2. **[P1] A restored wallet can show Success while future Drive backup is actually off.** After a successful recovery, [`restoreFromDriveBackup` discards the result of `setEnabled(true, launchResolution)`](https://github.com/cashubtc/wallet/blob/564ae1428f4301f306683b4482ba7d87e22ac340/android/app/src/main/java/com/cashu/me/Core/Wallet/WalletManager.kt#L1252-L1277), and [the UI unconditionally advances to `Success`](https://github.com/cashubtc/wallet/blob/564ae1428f4301f306683b4482ba7d87e22ac340/android/app/src/main/java/com/cashu/me/ui/restore/DriveRestoreStep.kt#L123-L135). This is reachable after a Block Store discovery: no Drive consent was needed to find the backup, so declining the post-restore consent rolls `driveBackupEnabled` back to false but does not fail or warn. iOS explicitly re-enables iCloud backup at restore completion. Treat re-arm failure as a visible “wallet restored, backup off” state with retry (or otherwise require an acknowledged outcome) rather than silently presenting complete parity.

3. **[P2] Offline/Drive failures are misclassified as “No backup found.”** [Every `DriveBackupException`, including the explicit network and HTTP errors, is collapsed to `DriveDetectResult.NotFound`](https://github.com/cashubtc/wallet/blob/564ae1428f4301f306683b4482ba7d87e22ac340/android/app/src/main/java/com/cashu/me/Core/GoogleDriveBackupService.kt#L234-L268), which then renders account-selection guidance instead of connection/error copy.
